items.title: Former Tekken Director Katsuhiro Harada Says His Next Game Will Be a ‘Surprise,’ But Not Outside Fans’ Expectations
items.description: Katsuhiro Harada, former leader of the Tekken franchise, is finally revealing some details about his next game currently in the works at his independent development house, VS Studio.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Katsuhiro Harada, former leader of the Tekken franchise, is finally revealing some details about his next game currently in the works at his independent development house, VS Studio.

Harada famously exited Bandai Namco earlier this year, leaving his decades-long post at the company as Tekken’s guiding force to make his own studio. A subsidiary of SNK, VS Studio has been slowly building its ranks over the last few months, snagging several former members of Tekken’s key development staff.

And while he’s been pretty quiet about what exactly VS Studio is cooking up, he shed some light on its current projects in a September 2026 interview with VideoGamesChronicle, and it’s tentatively looking like good news for fans of his previous games.

When asked if VS Studio’s next game would be a fighting game, or if the development house aims to be a “genre-agnostic” company, Harada had this to say: “What I can say is that there are some members who I have worked with in the past who have joined the company, but this is purely voluntary.

“...the title that we are creating has not been disclosed, but as I said earlier, I don’t want to betray our fans’ expectations. The game that we’re developing will be some kind of surprise, but rest assured, it is not something that is outside of expectations,” he answered.

While this statement doesn’t affirm anything, it does point to the fact that Harada is making something that is at least somewhat in the realm of what fans are expecting — and that, to us, sounds a lot like a fighting game. (It's also worth noting that Harada himself said he wanted to develop a new fighting game in an interview with Den-fami Nico Gamer after the news of VS Studio was first announced.) Whether it’s a totally new IP or a new installment of an existing franchise remains to be seen, but SNK’s chief publishing officer, Ozan Kocoglu, says VS Studio isn’t opposed to both making original titles and expanding on their previous works.

“I think it can be both. I don’t think we should be limited to one road or the other. I think Harada-san can bring a wealth of experience into supporting our existing IPs in growing in a different way, or going to the next stage alongside people like Oda-san. But at the same time, as SNK is growing to become much bigger and a new company, we also need fresh ideas,” he said.

“We also need to build new IP pillars that, you know, he could be working on, so that they can actually enrich the SNK portfolio beyond what we have. I definitely see Harada-san being able to do both, and it will depend on what he wants to do and how, and especially on which IP he could collaborate on with some of our development leads in the future.”

Kocoglu revealed that SNK is in a period of “aggressive growth,” saying the company needs a “fresh perspective” in order to keep moving forward. He also sees “no reason” why VS Studio should be a “one-off” for SNK, calling Harada a “great addition in terms of DNA with what we’ve been building so far.”

“But do we want to stop at only VS Studio? I don’t think that’s the idea. I think it’s going to be, okay, what are the new opportunities we can find in the market? How do we want to grow as a company? Personally, I think SNK has a strong DNA in action-related games. So anyone who makes an action-related project could potentially join us in the future on a case-by-case basis,” he added.

Harada went on to say that VS Studio has a “very high level of freedom,” and that while the team can “create anything we want,” they’re still beholden to what fans and players expect of them.

“What I want to protect is what I’m good at, as well as meet the expectations that my fans have. On top of that, I also want to collaborate with SNK. We can share the video game expertise that we have and enhance our strengths for both of us in terms of the ways to create video games. So, focusing on what I’m good at, keeping in mind player expectations as well, and having close collaboration with SNK,” he said.

Harada also opened up about his thoughts on the future of the Tekken franchise now that he’s left Bandai Namco, revealing that he’s been mentoring existing members of its staff while he works to grow VS Studio.

“I have no knowledge of what Tekken has in store after my departure, so I think it would be great if you could all reach out to Bandai Namco. For now, I can only speculate, like how fans are speculating as well. But one thing I can say is that I have been working hard to mentor the team members of Tekken, and I can guarantee that the members who are still working on it have evolved and grown. So I’m looking forward to the future of Tekken as a fan.”

Tekken 8, it seems, is joining the ranks of other mainline fighting games who are adding wildcard guest characters to their rosters, with Baki's Yujiro Hanma set to join the fight in early 2027. We got the chance to interview Tekken series chief producer Naoya Yasuda about why the team chose this character and how in the world they plan on balancing the game around the 'strongest man on earth' when he finally drops next year.

items.title: Zack Snyder Says 300 Is the ‘Gayest Movie Ever Made,' Defends The Last Photograph Amid Online Backlash
items.description: Zack Snyder is going viral off the heels of his latest movie, The Last Photograph, as well as his subsequent interview with Variety where he responded to the backlash against the film and made a few eyebrow-raising remarks about his previous work.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Zack Snyder is going viral off the heels of his latest movie, The Last Photograph, as well as his subsequent interview with Variety where he responded to the backlash against the film and made a few fascinating remarks about his previous work.

Reviews for Snyder’s The Last Photograph have been brutal. A swath of scathing opinions hit the net after its screening at the Toronto International Film Festival over the weekend, where Snyder joked that the audience in attendance might be the only ones to ever see it on the silver screen — and based on critical reception to the project, that might be a legitimate possibility.

For example, IGN gave the bloody action flick a 4 out of 10, calling it a “trudging revenge saga that points to self-critique” that’s “filled with big ideas that go nowhere.” Discourse online, however, has been far more vitriolic. According to Snyder himself, users on social media have been labeling him a “fascist” and a “homophobe” in the wake of these scalding reviews.

“Look, I’m famously surrounded by a particular discourse that happens around my movies. It’s incredibly charged. And I thought, for the smallest of moments, that because it’s a small movie and it’s really not that big of a deal, that it’d be allowed to exist on whatever level it is. What kind of noise does a tiny movie like this warrant from the world?” he said in a September 15 interview with Variety.

“This morning, I woke up to my X feed, and the discourse is incredibly energized by this battle. It’s like there’s a war going on — instantly — and on one hand, I don’t want to say it’s cool, but it has to exist in some ways. I don’t know why. The amount of energy and the amount of vitriol I find really incredible. ‘I want to kill Zack Snyder.’ ‘Zack Snyder is a fascist.’ ‘Zack Snyder is a homophobe.’ ‘Zack Snyder is a bisexual.’ …It’s ‘homoerotic’ and ‘transphobic’ and ‘fascist’ and all these things.”

To summarize the movie without spoiling things, The Last Photograph follows Ethan Black (Stuart Martin), a former DEA agent who searches the wilds of South America for his kidnapped niece and nephew after their parents are violently killed. He’s helped by a war photographer (Fra Fee) who witnessed the killings, and what follows is a violent tale of revenge that clearly left a sour taste in some viewers’ mouths, with some arguing that the brutality toward women and children displayed in the film borders on problematic.

“First of all, I would argue that the violence toward women and men is equal and that nobody is spared — men, women, children, everybody,” Snyder said of this criticism. “The justice that’s doled out in the movie is in the same way that a hurricane doles out justice. To try and superimpose morality over it and want the violence to mean something — the meaning is that violence doesn’t work and doesn’t get anything done.

“We’re all human. I guess in my feed, and this is just what my algorithm shows me, it’s a conversation. Even though I think it started out, ‘Zack Snyder sucks!’ ‘Fuck him!’ ‘You fascist!’ What happens now is, ‘You guys are f**king crazy. This is just a movie. Calm down.’ And look: Whether you like the movie or not, I’m not even commenting on that; but with me, it’s more clickable to say, ‘I hate Zack Snyder! He’s a fascist!’ than it is to say, ‘I saw the movie and it was cool.’ Nobody gives a fuck about that. And obviously, I’m not a fascist.”

Snyder then recalled a similarly strong reaction he received from attendees at the Berlin Film Festival after screening his action-packed historical hit 300, where the director claimed audiences literally booed the film and walked out. This particular anecdote resulted in a quote that’s since spread across social media like wildfire, and it's not hard to see why.

“They were saying it was ‘a disaster,’ ‘the worst movie ever’ and a ‘fascist’ movie. Then we had a press conference where they were asking me all these questions, like, ‘Are you a fascist filmmaker?’ …The hallmark question was when one of the guys said, ‘Are you pro-gay or pro-NRA? Which are you?’ And I said, ‘Look, I’ll be honest: I’m a tiny bit of both.’ But obviously I’m pro-gay. I made the gayest movie ever made,” Snyder said.

“...300 is one of the gayest movies ever made. I always go, ‘Look, there are few movies where people come in straight and come out gay, and 300 is one of them.’”

It remains to be seen whether or not The Last Photograph will find a distributor for an eventual theatrical release. For now, critical reception to the film has sparked curiosity from the general public, as well as a renewed interest in rewatching 300, which some fans are lovingly dubbing the “apex” of his filmography in retrospect. In stark contrast to his latest offering, IGN scored 300 a 9.9 out of 10 at the time, calling it a "one-of-a-kind masterpiece."

Image Credits: Warner Bros. Pictures

items.title: Casino Royale Is Returning to Theaters for the Film's 20th Anniversary
items.description: Daniel Craig's first James Bond film, Casino Royale, is returning to theaters very soon for the film's 20th anniversary.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Daniel Craig's first James Bond film, Casino Royale, is returning to theaters very soon for the film's 20th anniversary.

Amazon MGM Studios confirmed the news today with a poster confirming that the iconic 007 film will return to theaters worldwide this October. A firm release date wasn't provided and it's hard to predict, since the film originally released on November 17, 2006 in the United States, so this anniversary screening is happening a bit earlier than one might expect. However, given how stacked November is with film releases, October is likely a better choice anyways.

Casino Royale was a watershed moment for the Bond franchise, as the Pierce Brosnan era largely crashed and burned by the end of its run. The series was seeking something that could modernize and refresh itself for audiences, leading to a more grounded, gritty, and raw take on the MI6 spy. Despite doubts that he could pull it off, Craig turned in a captivating performance that was both charming and intimidating. Perhaps even more notably, he gave Bond a bit more depth than ever before, and the filmmakers took advantage of his vibrant blue eyes for some really emotional moments toward the end of the film.

To celebrate its 20th anniversary, CASINO ROYALE returns to the big screen worldwide. pic.twitter.com/dOrpP3ZCwb

— James Bond (@007) September 15, 2026

Casino Royale kicked off a legendary five-film run for Craig, and although not all of them were slam dunks, they cleaned up at the box office and revitalized a character that some fans had begun to count out. Craig's time as 007 came to an end in 2021 with No Time to Die, and now, all eyes are on the future of the character. Amazon is actively developing the next Bond film with director Denis Villeneuve, with an expectation that it will shoot shortly after he finishes Dune Part 3.

Casting for the next James Bond has been underway since the spring, and rumors suggest the producers have already found their man. The first draft of the script is also complete, according to writer Steven Knight, suggesting the film is making strong progress. The next Bond is expected to be announced by the end of the year, and some fans think this re-release may help lead into that. We'll have to wait and see what happens, but it's an exciting time to be a Bond fan.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass September 2026 Wave 2 Lineup Announced
items.description: Microsoft has announced the Xbox Game Pass September 2027 Wave 2 lineup, and it includes Dune Awakening, plus Minecraft Dungeons 2 and Gears of War: E-Day for Ultimate and PC subscribers.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Microsoft has announced the Xbox Game Pass September 2027 Wave 2 lineup, and it includes Dune Awakening, plus Minecraft Dungeons 2 and Gears of War: E-Day for Ultimate and PC subscribers.

Sandy survival RPG Dune: Awakening is amongst this month's biggest additions, and lands for Game Pass Premium, PC and Ultimate subscribers on September 22. PC and Ultimate subscribers will meanwhile get day-one access to Minecraft Dungeons 2 and Gears of War: E-Day on September 29 and October 6, respectively.

Also worth a look this month are comicbook beat 'em up Marvel Cosmic Invasion, sci-fi puzzler Planet of Lana 2, Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 and Ninja Gaiden 4, all of which join Xbox Game Pass Premium. If you've yet to try it already, Premium subscribers also get to play Keeper, just as the game also pops up on PlayStation 5.

Other titles on offer include bike-racing party game Ultimate Sheep Raccoon, sci-fi horror Routine, action RPG roguelike Kernel Hearts, dark fairytale Metroidvania Well Dweller and 2.5D roguelite beat 'em up Mad King Redemption. Anything tickle your fancy?

Xbox Game Pass September 2026 Wave 2 lineup:

  • RuneScape: Dragonwilds (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, and PC) – September 15, Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Marvel Cosmic Invasion (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, Handheld, and PC) – September 16, now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Planet of Lana II (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, Handheld, and PC) – September 16, now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Routine (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) – September 16, now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Ultimate Sheep Raccoon (Cloud, Console, and PC) – September 16, now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Kernel Hearts (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, and PC) – September 17, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • Ninja Gaiden 4 (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, Handheld, and PC) – September 17, now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Dune: Awakening (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, Handheld, and PC) – September 22, Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Well Dweller (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) – September 22, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • Mad King Redemption (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, Handheld, and PC) – September 23, Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) – September 25, now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Minecraft Dungeons 2 (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) – September 29, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • Keeper (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, and PC) – October 2, now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Gears of War: E-Day (Xbox Series X/S, Handheld, PC, and Cloud) – October 6, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

As always, whenever Microsoft giveth, it also taketh away. A number of games leave Game Pass this month, including the rather British-feeling Fallout-like, Atomfall. Be sure to play that before it departs, as well as everything else listed below:

Games leaving Xbox Game Pass on September 30:

  • Atomfall (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Little Nightmares 2 Enhanced Edition (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Little Rocket Lab (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Sifu (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • SOPA Tale of the Stolen Potato (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Sworn (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Terminull Brigade (Cloud, Console, and PC)

items.title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's Nintendo Switch 2 Version Delayed to Early 2027
items.description: Cold Iron Studios, developer of the recently released four-player co-op PvE sequel Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2, has announced that the Nintendo Switch 2 version has been pushed back to early 2027. It was originally planned to ship this month.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Cold Iron Studios, developer of the recently released four-player co-op PvE sequel Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2, has announced that the Nintendo Switch 2 version has been pushed back to early 2027. It was originally planned to ship this month.

"After careful consideration, we now plan to release it natively on Switch 2 in early 2027," the studio said in a statement. "This extra time will help the team deliver the best possible version for the hardware. Thank you for your patience and understanding. In the meantime, the team at Cold Iron remains aggressively focused on tuning Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 to be the best possible experience for every player."

IGN gave the PC, Xbox, and PlayStation version of Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 a 7 out of 10, saying in part, "Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 isn’t going to make you leave a co-op shooter you already love at the altar, but it is a good time with friends."

items.title: Fable Developer Explains Why Xbox 'Protected' the Project Over Its Long Development Cycle, Amid Layoffs and Studio Closures Elsewhere
items.description: Fable maker Playground Games has detailed how its upcoming RPG survived a decade in development, amid layoffs and studio closures across the rest of Xbox.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Fable maker Playground Games has detailed how its upcoming RPG survived a decade in development, amid layoffs and studio closures across the rest of Xbox.

Early work on building Fable's team began in 2017, just a year after Microsoft shut down classic Fable maker Lionhead Studios. 10 years on, Playground Games' Fable will finally launch after a mammoth development, into a very different gaming landscape.

When work on Fable began, Xbox was still to acquire We Happy Few maker Compulsion Games, Psychonauts studio Double Fine, State of Decay developer Undead Labs, or Hellblade team Ninja Theory — all companies it subsequently cast adrift this summer. Xbox was yet to set up The Initiative, the team it pumped millions into for the purposes of making Perfect Dark, then closed after 7 years with nothing to show for it. There was no sign Xbox would splash out $7.5 billion on Bethesda (including id, MachineGames, and the now-divested Tango Gameworks). And there was certainly no inkling it would drop $68.7 billion on Activision Blizzard.

Likewise, there was no telling that Microsoft's many acquisitions would be followed by successive waves of layoffs. 1,900 jobs were slashed in January 2024, many from the newly-acquired Activision Blizzard, while at least 650 staff were let go later that year, and Redfall maker Arkane Austin was closed. Last year, meanwhile, 9,000 staff departed Microsoft as the company pivoted towards AI spending, wiping out The Initiative and scores of workers from both Forza Motorsport team Turn 10 and veteran British outfit Rare, which saw its meandering work on Everwild ended after more than a decade.

And there were this year's layoffs, the first to come from new Xbox boss Asha Sharma. These will ultimately end up hitting 3,200 workers, with significant doubt now placed on the future of Marvel's Blade maker Arkane Lyon.

So, how did Fable survive all of that? Speaking to The Guardian, director Ralph Fulton explained that the Fable franchise simply remained "vital" to Xbox.

"I genuinely think Fable is an important game," Fulton said. "What has protected us over a long development cycle is that so many people within Xbox view Fable as vital to the DNA of the platform.

"I would go a step further and say it's important to video games as a whole," he continued. "It offers a combination of elements that simply doesn't exist anywhere else."

Video games do not typically get the luxury of having decade-long development cycles, and it does feel like Fable is one of Xbox's few core brands that remain central to the platform, alongside Halo, Forza and Gears of War. Compared to these, it's perhaps not a surprise to see Xbox push on with the game's lengthy road to release, even as it ditched untested ideas like Everwild (which seemed some way from release still, even after a decade in the oven). And then there's the fact that, while one team within Playground was busy building Fable, another was just as busy pumping out its hugely-successful and well-regarded Forza Horizon games, which will certainly have helped pay the bills.

Whatever the case, we're very happy Fable is now nearing the end of its journey — and looking forward to playing it when it finally arrives on February 23, 2027.

items.title: Rockstar Games Begins Teasing GTA 6's Soundtrack With Travis Scott, Future, Morgan Wallen, and More
items.description: Rockstar Games has begun teasing the soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto 6 with new artwork from Future, Travis Scott, and other artists.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar Games has begun teasing the soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto 6 with new artwork from Future, Travis Scott, and other artists.

Travis Scott, Future, and Morgan Wallen have all posted zoomed-in pictures of a larger piece of artwork from Grand Theft Auto 6. Scott's image featured a woman's heeled feet and was paired with a caption mentioning Rockstar, while Wallen's was a caption-less image of a pool ladder in Rockstar's art style. Many assumed that these were all teasing GTA 6 in some capacity, and that was confirmed once Future uploaded a picture of a sports car repping a Leonida license plate. Metro Boomin and Yung Lean also posted the same image as Future on their respective profiles.

Argentine hip hop duo CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso also posted their own image, which featured a yacht. The same image was shared by Fred Again and an account that claims to be affiliated with PinkPantheress, leading some to speculate that the artists sharing duplicate images are actually collaborating on the same songs together.

Presumably, there will be more of these posts from other artists throughout the day, so we will continue to keep this article updated as more images roll in.

It's likely that all of these singers will have music in the game, but it's unclear if they have larger roles as characters in the game or radio hosts. Dr. Dre was prominently featured as a character in GTA Online, Phil Colins was a character in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, and a number of comedians like Ricky Gervais have appeared in the flesh in games like GTA 4, so there's precedent for them to appear as actual characters. Actor Stephen Root also confirmed his long speculated role as Brian Heder in GTA 6 earlier this week, though seemingly through a slip-up rather than a planned reveal.

This appears to be just one part of Rockstar Games' massive marketing push for GTA 6, which properly kicked off this summer with pre-orders and an extensive gameplay reveal that debuted on Netflix. Rockstar is expected to keep its foot on the gas until launch, which is almost exactly two months away now.

items.title: Apex Legends Art Director Says Street Fighter 6 Pushed Devs to Give Characters the 'Thickest Thighs' They've Ever Had
items.description: Apex Legends art director Alisa Rastorgueva revealed that the developers pushed the limits of the game’s character models so far for its collaboration with Street Fighter 6 that its heroes became “thicker” than ever.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Apex Legends art director Alisa Rastorgueva says developers pushed the limits of the game’s character models so far for its collaboration with Street Fighter 6 that its heroes became “thicker” than ever.

Street Fighter 6 is coming to Apex Legends with special character skins, a decked-out POI, an ambitious Wildcard Takover, weapon skins, and more on September 22.

To celebrate, a handful of Legends are getting the Street Fighter treatment, transforming them into characters from Capcom’s beloved fighting game franchise: Sparrow is Ryu; Alter is Chun-Li; Mirage is Luke; Caustic is Blanka; Wattson is Cammy; Gibraltar is Akuma; Bangalore is Elena; and Pathfinder is Dhalsim.

Each fighter in this delightful selection of characters boasts a striking silhouette with the muscles to match (they are martial artists, after all) — and that was something that challenged the art team when it came to literally breaking the mold of their Legends to make them look like their Street Fighter counterparts.

In a closed session with the media, Apex Legends art director Alisa Rastorgueva revealed that these Street Fighter skins were so muscular that the Legends now have the thickest thighs they’ve ever made for the game.

“There’s always a new challenge with every collab that we do, and it’s always different,” she told us. “With Gundam, it was trying to fit our Legends into these big mechs. For Street Fighter, a big challenge was trying to find a balance between pushing the body types, especially the muscle definition. All of us know that Street Fighter characters are muscular and their proportions are pushed a lot. We tried to do that, as well. Our legends have some of the thickest thighs we’ve ever done. To take an IP with that much history behind it and put it into Apex Legends — our game is semi-realistic, it definitely has a different visual style than Street Fighter has in a lot of their games, and for us, that was one of our biggest challenges. But it was a fun one.”

She also delved into the selection process for choosing these specific Street Fighter characters, explaining that there were many fighters the team considered bringing into the game, but only a few made sense to pair with their Legends.

“It’s just what worked best for this collaboration,” she said. “All of the pairings we do are a collaborative effort between our departments and the IP holder. We definitely wanted to have the Street Fighter characters represented well and be recognizable within the game, and this worked best with Alter and Sparrow. You can see characters like Chun-Li and Ryu very clearly when it’s designed on them versus other Legends. We do test characters for all the pairings, and we ended up working with [Sparrow and Alter] once again.”

Senior technical game designer Chris Ruvolo added that it wasn’t just a matter of physicality, but of gameplay, as well; putting a grappler like Zangief in a first-person shooter like Apex Legends wouldn’t really make sense for the type of game it is, despite how cool it’d be.

“There were a lot that we wanted to add that we couldn't,” he admitted. “We really wanted to highlight characters from Street Fighter 6 specifically. Unfortunately, I wish we could do the full roster, but we weren’t able to. We highlighted some of the characters that worked best for us and our IP partner.

“Me and my manager played a lot of Street Fighter 6,” he continued. “We got all the fighter passes and played around with them to see what would work best for Apex. It was kinda tough figuring out what characters to bring in, since Apex is primarily a shooter. You can't have a fighter who focuses on grapples like Zangief. We had to go with characters who were projectile-based or had area of effect attacks; those were at the top of our list. The creative process was, ‘What are some characters that players are gonna recognize? Which will fit well within Apex’s gameplay?’”

You can brawl it out in the new Wildcard Takeover, punch destructible cars, and even pull off a Hadouken when Street Fighter hurricane-kicks its way into Apex Legends on September 22.

items.title: Apex Legends VS Street Fighter Brings Chun-Li, Ryu, Akuma, and More to the Outlands
items.description: Street Fighter is coming to Apex Legends on September 22, bringing its high-kicking action to the first-person battle royale with special skins, a decked-out POI, a Wildcard Takeover, and more.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Street Fighter is coming to Apex Legends on September 22, bringing its high-kicking action to the first-person battle royale with special skins, a decked-out POI, a Wildcard Takeover, and more.

This collaboration hurricane-kicks its way into the Outlands on Tuesday, September 22 at 10am PT / 1pm ET. We’ve outlined everything you can expect from Apex Legends’ Street Fighter makeover below.

Skins, Mythic Cosmetics, Emotes & More

Players will have the chance to nab eight Iconic Skins in the Reward Shop that transform their Legends into characters from Capcom’s beloved fighting game franchise, as well as one Epic Skin for Lifeline as Li-Fen, Chun-Li’s protege in Street Fighter 6’s World Tour story mode. We’ve included a list of all these characters below, as well as comments about the skins from Apex Legends’ art director, Alisa Rastorgueva, from a closed session with the media:

● Sparrow as Ryu: “We’re really thinking about personality, playstyle, silhouette when matching our Apex Legends with their Street Fighter counterparts. Sparrow felt the closest to Ryu's grisly self in Street Fighter 6 specifically, and we really wanted to push the muscle definition for this skin.”

● Alter as Chun-Li: “We wanted to make sure Alter could do Chun-Li justice. We pushed the silhouettes of these models and bodies.”

● Bangalore as Elena: “

● Mirage as Luke: “Luke is Street Fighter 6’s breakout character, so we really wanted to feature him. Mirage felt like an obvious match in terms of personality, since they never take themselves seriously.”

● Gibraltar as Akuma: “This was definitely a fun skin for Gibby. His size and silhouette gave us a good canvas to bring that to life.”

● Wattson as Cammy: “They really complement each other. How Wattson operates matches well with Cammy’s fighting style.”

● Caustic as Blanka: “Blanka is big, unpredictable, and terrifying. One detail we are really proud of here are Caustic’s canisters: As you can see here, they feature electric eels that we hope fans catch and appreciate.”

● Pathfinder as Dhalsim: "Figuring out how to put Dahlsim's design on a robot was definitely a challenge.”

Eight new Legendary Street Fighter 6-themed weapon skins are also available in the Reward Shop:

● R-99

● EVA-8

● Flatline

● Volt

● Scout

● Mozambique

● Sentinel

● Peacekeeper

Other goodies include two new Skydive Emotes (one of them is a Tatsumaki), Holosprays, stickers (these include all characters in Street Fighter 6’s base roster), badges, trackers, and frames.

To really get players into the Street Fighter spirit, the devs at Respawn have lovingly prepared a new Hadouken Universal Melee cosmetic that includes a matching Deathbox. This allows players to literally throw out a Hadouken projectile in the middle of battle; just don’t fall prey to the Dark Hadou!

Remixed Olympus POI

Olympus is getting a Street Fighter makeover; the entire area has been decked out in bright colors, graffiti, giant Blanka-chan balloons, and even silver statues of the eight characters featured as skins in this collaboration. Punch Trucks are scattered throughout the POI, which players can beat up using melee attacks to earn Fight Gauge tokens in traditional Street Fighter fashion.

That’s not all; Pathfinder’s Fight Night has been transformed into Luke’s Gym, featuring arcade cabinets, Street Fighter 6-branded punching bags, a weight rack, and of course, Luke’s signature blue and orange colors. There’s even a massive screen surrounding the entire area featuring Ryu and Chun-Li facing off, which will loom over the match in its entirety.

“Remixing Olympus for this takeover was all about immersing players in fighting game culture, world director Eduardo Agostini said. “Building off what we learned on maps like Night City E-District, we wanted Olympus to feel like a living Street Fighter stage. For the Street Fighter 6 collaboration especially, we kept thinking of how we could inject that high-energy arcade feel directly into the map. …We’re really excited for players to explore every corner of this map and feel the energy that the team poured into it.”

Wildcard Takeover Explained

The Apex Legends x Street Fighter collab also features a Wildcard Takeover that transforms the first-person shooter into an all-out brawl. Rather than firing bullets at other players, you’ll use your Street Fighter skills to punch and kick your opponents. For this mode, the devs at Respawn cleaned up the game’s melee to let players perform fluid combos, which will fill your Fighter Gauge. Collecting tokens throughout the area will also fill your gauge, allowing you to enter Fighter Form, a third-person combat mode with new Tactical and Ultimate abilities, movement, and blocking capabilities.

Titled Apex KO, players will need to select one of four fighters before entering the match as either Ryu, Chun-Li, Dhalsim and Akuma. If you don’t make a choice, one will be selected for you. When you enter Fighter Form, your abilities will be replaced with skills that suit each Street Fighter character. Some of these are listed below:

  • Ryu: Shin Shoryuken, Dash, Hadouken.
    • (You can lock onto targets to hit them with the hadouken but it won’t do exploding damage.)
  • Chun-Li: Double-jump, Kikouken, Kikosho, and faster melee attack speed.
  • Dhalsim: Increased melee range, Teleportation, Yoga sunburst.
  • Akuma: Gohadouken, Shun Goku Satsu, Raging Demon, Demon Mode.

The final round is called the Showdown, where any downed or respawning players rejoin the fight to throw hands until one squad is left standing.

“At its core, Apex is built on competition,” Chris Ruvolo, senior technical game designer for Apex Legends, said in a statement. “Translating Street Fighter 6’s mechanics into a third-person Battle Royale experience was about finding those synergies in their shared competitive DNA. Balancing the four Fighter Gear kits was such a fun opportunity to give players highly expressive tools like Hadokens, wall-runs and Yoga Teleports without compromising Apex’s core gameplay and competitive integrity. The final Showdown round distills that drive into a high-stakes brawl where clutch execution decides who survives.”

Olympus is getting a Street Fighter makeover; the entire area has been decked out in bright colors, graffiti, giant Blanka-chan balloons, and even silver statues of the eight characters featured as skins in this collaboration. Punch Trucks are scattered throughout the POI, which players can beat up using melee attacks to earn Fight Gauge tokens in traditional Street Fighter fashion.

That’s not all; Pathfinder’s Fight Night has been transformed into Luke’s Gym, featuring arcade cabinets, Street Fighter 6-branded punching bags, a weight rack, and of course, Luke’s signature blue and orange colors. There’s even a massive screen surrounding the entire area featuring Ryu and Chun-Li facing off, which will loom over the match in its entirety.

“Remixing Olympus for this takeover was all about immersing players in fighting game culture, world director Eduardo Agostini said. “Building off what we learned on maps like Night City E-District, we wanted Olympus to feel like a living Street Fighter stage. For the Street Fighter 6 collaboration especially, we kept thinking of how we could inject that high-energy arcade feel directly into the map. …We’re really excited for players to explore every corner of this map and feel the energy that the team poured into it.”

Wildcard Takeover Explained

The Apex Legends x Street Fighter collab also features a Wildcard Takeover that transforms the first-person shooter into an all-out brawl. Rather than firing bullets at other players, you’ll use your Street Fighter skills to punch and kick your opponents. For this mode, the devs at Respawn cleaned up the game’s melee to let players perform fluid combos, which will fill your Fighter Gauge. Collecting tokens throughout the area will also fill your gauge, allowing you to enter Fighter Form, a third-person combat mode with new Tactical and Ultimate abilities, movement, and blocking capabilities.

Titled Apex KO, players will need to select one of four fighters before entering the match as either Ryu, Chun-Li, Dhalsim and Akuma. If you don’t make a choice, one will be selected for you. When you enter Fighter Form, your abilities will be replaced with skills that suit each Street Fighter character. Some of these are listed below:

  • Ryu: Shin Shoryuken, Dash, Hadouken.
    • (You can lock onto targets to hit them with the hadouken but it won’t do exploding damage.)
  • Chun-Li: Double-jump, Kikouken, Kikosho, and faster melee attack speed.
  • Dhalsim: Increased melee range, Teleportation, Yoga sunburst.
  • Akuma: Gohadouken, Shun Goku Satsu, Raging Demon, Demon Mode.

The final round is called the Showdown, where any downed or respawning players rejoin the fight to throw hands until one squad is left standing.

“At its core, Apex is built on competition,” Chris Ruvolo, senior technical game designer for Apex Legends, said in a statement. “Translating Street Fighter 6’s mechanics into a third-person Battle Royale experience was about finding those synergies in their shared competitive DNA. Balancing the four Fighter Gear kits was such a fun opportunity to give players highly expressive tools like Hadokens, wall-runs and Yoga Teleports without compromising Apex’s core gameplay and competitive integrity. The final Showdown round distills that drive into a high-stakes brawl where clutch execution decides who survives.”

items.title: Harry Potter TV Series Casts Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle and Colin Creevey
items.description: HBO's Harry Potter TV series has found its Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle and Colin Creevey, with Rafe Spall cast as Ron's dad.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
HBO's Harry Potter TV series has found its Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle, and Colin Creevey, with Rafe Spall cast as Ron's dad.

Spall currently stars in Apple TV series Trying, though has also had roles in Life of Pi, Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom, Men in Black: International, and Black Mirror.

Portrayed by Mark Williams in the original Harry Potter movies, Arthur Weasley is the good-natured patriarch of the Weasley family, and a recurring character through the Harry Potter series from the second book onwards.

It is Arthur's love of Muggle objects that ensures Harry and Ron can get to Hogwarts in an enchanted Ford Anglia, and in later stories Arthur's position in the Ministry of Magic allows Harry to hear the inner workings of the wizarding world as Voldemort ascends to power.

Other roles announced today include ghostly schoolgirl Moaning Myrtle and the photography-obsessed Colin Creevey. Both have small roles throughout the series, though first pop up in Chamber of Secrets as victims of a mysterious creature slithering around Hogwarts castle. Here, the pair will be played by newcomers Molly Hewitt-Richards and Jasper Ambrose, respectively.

Earlier this month, HBO announced a trio of other key roles for its second season of its Harry Potter adaptation, which now has actors cast for Tom Riddle (AKA the young Lord Voldemort), Dobby the house-elf and a new face for Ginny Weasley. Game of Thrones star Kit Harington will play Gilderoy Lockhart, meanwhile, filling in for Tom Hoult who dropped out due to a recent filming delay.

This month also brought our best look yet at the series' upcoming first season, including a peek at Quidditch, Professor Snape and the Sorting Hat. That's due to begin airing at Christmas this year, with the now-filming second season expected to follow in late 2027 or 2028.

Images credit: HBO.

items.title: Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons Doesn't Have Waypoints Because the Devs Want Players to 'Figure Things Out' for Themselves
items.description: The developers of Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons have said they avoided putting waypoints into the game because they want players to actually explore.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The developers of Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons have said they avoided putting waypoints into the game because they want players to actually explore.

The open-world single-player action-adventure goes easy on the hand-holding by ditching traditional quest markers that guide players directly from one story section to the next. While it does have a compass on the top of the screen — which you can turn off — the player is left to work out where to go by exploring, talking to NPCs, and thinking about what to do next.

Dominic Guay, General Manager at Invoke Studios, told IGN at gamescom 2026 the decision was all about wanting to encourage exploration. “We wanted them to engage with the world, to figure things out and feel that when they found things, it was based on their actions and not just blindly trusting a waypoint,” he said.

Guay and the rest of the developers at Invoke have experience making open world games that include waypoints, such as Ubisoft’s Watch Dogs series. But this time around, for Warlock, they wanted to do things differently.

“The core team on this game have worked on other open world games before and we've done the, let's say, the heavy-handed guiding approach before,” Guay said. “What ends up happening at some point — and it's normal — a lot of players will just follow blindly the waypoint, and then you lose that agency, you lose that feeling of curiosity because you're like, well, why even bother? And so we didn't want to go there. We wanted the player to explore.”

To that end, Warlock has a Mystery system that are triggered when players take certain actions, typically in a settlement. The idea is players will uncover mysteries by exploring, talking to NPCs, and gathering information, rather than following a quest market to where the Mystery officially kicks off.

“There are multiple entry points,” Guay explained. “They're kind of harder for us to do in that way, but we love that challenge. Not only are there multiple entry points, but depending on how you stumble upon them, it might change how you interact with them, meaning that maybe you could have found actually you can chance upon that Mystery from a completely different place and then it'll lead you toward that settlement, and you'll know before coming in there's something fishy going on here. So then you'll approach that settlement differently than in this case where you learn it from within.

"Some [Mysteries] are a little bit more straightforward, some are a little bit more deep and requires more engagement and exploration, but that's really how they're built."

Video game hand-holding is of course a hot topic right now with the release of PlayStation 5 exclusive Marvel’s Wolverine, which has been criticized for its now infamous “fart gas” — the depiction of Logan’s scent trail as he tracks other characters, chases down enemies, and sniffs out collectibles. Some want to be able to turn it off.

The two games are very different, of course. Warlock is an open-world action adventure with emergent gameplay that comes from its unique magic system, whereas Wolverine is a linear action adventure with combat that takes place in constrained areas. Insomniac’s effort isn’t a quest marker sort of game, but it is interesting to hear Invoke’s philosophy when it comes to player hand-holding, and how it set out to avoid it.

items.title: Wolverine Developer Insomniac Promises to 'Further Refine the Player Experience' Based on Feedback
items.description: Marvel’s Wolverine developer Insomniac has said it’s planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback, while insisting it’s “incredibly proud” of the game.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Marvel’s Wolverine developer Insomniac has said it’s planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback, while insisting it’s “incredibly proud” of the game.

Wolverine is currently sitting on a 77 Metascore, with IGN’s Marvel’s Wolverine review returning a 6/10. We said: “Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay.”

In a post on social media to celebrate the launch of the game this week, Insomniac said it was “actively engaged” with players to gather feedback, and promised changes.

Here’s the statement in full:

“It’s finally here — the launch day for Marvel’s Wolverine! We’re grateful to everyone who has helped us reach this special moment. Players around the world are beginning their journey with Logan and we’re excited to learn about everyone’s experiences playing the game.

“We’re incredibly proud of what the team has created. We’re also actively engaged with our player community and gathering feedback to further refine the player experience.

“We deeply appreciate our players’ passion, support, and time spent with Logan. We’re raising our claws in tribute, and can’t wait to hear about your own adventures playing Marvel’s Wolverine.”

The question for players is, to what extent can Insomniac “further refine” the gameplay? Perhaps it’s planning to add depth to the combat, which is at the centre of many of the review complaints. Or maybe it plans to add variety to the play spaces in some way. Given the linearity of Marvel’s Wolverine's gameplay and the tight story it tells, it’s hard to envisage significant changes here.

However, one aspect Insomniac may be looking at is Wolverine’s infamous “fart gas,” which has become the butt of online jokes in recent weeks. Some have called for Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game amid complaints about handholding.

The debate around this was rekindled following the publication of Marvel’s Wolverine reviews online last week, with The Washington Post journalist Gene Park calling the scent trail “fart gas” because of the way it appears behind characters Logan follows.

Jean Grey’s fart gas trail is NOT part of the navigation assist option. i turned it on and there’s another green line that tells you where to go. mission waypoint (yellow marker) is on as well and THAT can be turned off.

2nd pic i turn off the options and the gas stays. it seems… https://t.co/XSBsGa6Xj0 pic.twitter.com/cKs9uTPSG0

— Gene Park (@GenePark) September 10, 2026

There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either.

This in turn led some to believe the scent trail is always on in-game, and so have called on Insomniac to add in the ability to turn it off. But, ahead of Wolverine’s release, Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to explain that Logan's scent trail is baked into the way the mutant's powers work.

“The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.”

Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides, some have said Logan's scent trails remove any potential skill required for chase sequences and any joy of discovery in exploration. Could Insomniac be prepared to make changes to the way Wolverine’s scent trail works?

The only other potential changes I can think of that wouldn't require a significant and costly rework of the foundations of the game itself have to do with New Game Plus content. Wolverine has New Game Plus day one, and indeed Insomniac has insisted there's plenty for players to do once they've beaten the story. But maybe there's scope to add some more activities or challenges for players to sink their claws into.

items.title: Wardogs Sells 2 Million Copies in 5 Days as Early Access Shooter Blows Up on Steam
items.description: Wardogs’ incredible success has seen it sell 2 million copies after just five days of release.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Wardogs’ incredible success has seen it sell 2 million copies after just five days of release.

Bulkhead’s tactical first-person shooter released in early access form on Steam on September 10 and was an instant hit, reaching a peak of 428,666 concurrent players and becoming one of the most-played games on Valve’s platform. It sold 1 million copies on day one, and 1.25 million by day two.

“Thank you all. Beyond humbled,” Bulkhead said in a post on social media. “We made a game we wanted to play with friends. Watching you play it with yours has been the best.”

User reviews are now ‘Very Positive’ after initial complaints around launch problems. That appears to be done and dusted now, with players getting on with the game and having fun. A number of gameplay clips showing Wardogs shenanigans have gone viral (players are even avoiding Wardogs’ Lonestar faction over a perception that they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games).

Bulkhead has said it expects Wardogs to remain in early access for 1-2 years, with a console version planned for 2028. “We are adamant that we do not want to be in Early Access for a long time,” its Steam page reads.

“That time is planned for expanding content, improving systems, refining balance, and responding to player feedback. The exact duration may change depending on how development and community feedback evolves.”

“The full version of Wardogs, whenever it comes out, will be “broader and more polished” than the early access release, Bulkhead has said. Because of this, expect the price of the game to go up when the full release comes out “to reflect the more complete experience.”

“Early access players benefit from getting in at a lower price and helping shape the game as it develops,” Bulkhead has said.

As for the expansion of the game, expect more maps, weapons, vehicles, and gameplay variety. The priority now is building “deeper reasons to play beyond individual matches.”

“We plan to develop more in depth progression systems, a stronger seasonal meta game, and additional systems that reward players for the time and impact they bring to a match, whether through combat, support, or logistics,” Bulkhead said.

“Alongside this, we plan broader gameplay additions such as new vehicle types including fighter jets, expanded weapon categories, additional objective variations, and continued improvements to the core Wardogs experience.

“Throughout Early Access and beyond, our ongoing priority will always be improving balance, performance, and stability.”

items.title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer Reboot Cancellation Means Fans Will Never Discover if Buffy and Angel Ended Up Together, Sarah Michelle Gellar Jokes
items.description: Hulu's shock cancellation of its Buffy the Vampire Slayer reboot means that fans will never discover if Buffy and Angel ultimately ended up together.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Hulu's shock cancellation of its Buffy the Vampire Slayer reboot means that fans will never discover if Buffy and Angel ultimately ended up together.

That's according to the Slayer herself, Sarah Michelle Gellar, who reunited with Angel actor David Boreanaz last night at the Emmy Awards. As the pair took the stage together to present a prize, the duo chatted about their characters and also paid tribute to their trio of co-stars who have passed away over the last couple of years.

"You know Sarah, I always thought Buffy and Angel would end up together," Boreanaz said at one point.

"Well, I guess we won't find out," Gellar responded, in a pointed comment that drew laughs from the room, as the audience realized this was a not-so-veiled reference to Hulu's series being scrapped.

Gellar was heavily involved in plans for a soft reboot of the cult series, now updated for the modern day in a fresh version of Sunnydale, and with a new young Slayer as its lead. Gellar herself would have appeared as a recurring character, and other Buffy alumni would have made guest appearances (Spike actor James Marsters has said he expected to pop up at some point, though likely not until the show's second season).

Could Angel have appeared too at some point, in order to wrap up the series' infamous love triangle? Or would Spike and Buffy fans continue to think their true pairing had a chance? As Gellar says, it seems we won't find out.

Sarah Michelle Gellar & David Boreanaz have a Buffy reunion and give nod to late cast members Anthony Head, Michelle Trachtenberg and Nicholas Brendon #Emmys pic.twitter.com/zpLcscG3NR

— Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 15, 2026

Various reports have suggested that the reboot's original pilot script — the one that has now partially leaked — featured only a brief appearance by Gellar at the end of the episode. While her character was clearly being set up to appear in an expanded role in later stories (and it perhaps makes sense that the pilot focused on establishing its new cast) Hulu apparently balked at Buffy herself only getting a single line, and asked for a do-over with far more screemtime for Gellar.

Gellar previously pinned the reboot's cancellation squarely on a single executive who she claimed had boasted about never being a Buffy fan. Reports have suggested Hulu remains keen to try another attempt at a Buffy reboot in a few years, though it currently seems unlikely for Gellar to be convinced again — meaning Angel and Buffy fans will just have to wonder what could have been.

"Before we move on to the award, David and I would like to acknowledge that it has been a tough two years for our beloved cast and crew," Gellar concluded, in a clear nod to the recent passing of Anthony Stewart Head (Giles), Nicholas Brendon (Xander) and Michelle Trachtenberg (Dawn). "We feel very lucky to have known and worked with such amazing people."

items.title: Trump Calls AI Safety Warnings a 'Hoax,' Refuses to Back Guardrails Anthropic and OpenAI Insist Are Needed to Help Prevent Human Extinction
items.description: Donald Trump has called AI safety warnings a “hoax” in response to claims the technology has a greater than 10% chance of killing all humans.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Donald Trump has called AI safety warnings a “hoax” in response to claims the technology has a greater than 10% chance of killing all humans.

Last week, an Anthropic safety researcher claimed there is a greater than 10% chance that AI “could kill all humans” within the next decade, admitting there is no coordinated plan to prevent it from happening.

Since then, the bosses of the major AI tech companies have called for a global slowdown in AI development, and requested the U.S. government impose guardrails — such as a kill switch that can be checked by a third party — on AI. But in a series of posts on Truth Social, Trump made his position clear.

Trump said there was a “SICK conspiracy” underway to undermine AI development, and insisted he alone would prevent AI from going rogue. He compared AI safety concerns to what he called the “Global Warming Scam,” and called for an acceleration in data center development.

“The people that say AI is going to destroy the World, and that Data Centers are bad for your neighborhood, are the same people that said, just a short time ago, that the World would be extinguished by ‘Climate Change,’” Trump wrote. “That HOAX never worked out for them, and now they’re on to the next one.”

The U.S. president called himself "the Hoax Buster,” saying the only "guardrails" needed for AI was a "strong and smart" president.

Nvidia boss Jensen Huang — who is at the heart of the AI boom — took a phone call from Trump while he was on-stage at a conference. Huang, himself an opponent of AI regulation, put Trump on speakerphone for a conversation that has since gone viral on social media.

“I’m telling you it’s all a hoax,” Trump said as Huang help up a microphone to a phone. “Data centers are great and they make people wealthy and they make states wealthy. It’s the oil of the next 20-25 years. It’s bigger than the internet. They’re just playing right into the hands of a lot of people who don’t want to see it happen. They could be political people. It could also be China. And we’re not going to let that happen.

“The robots are not gonna be taking over the world. That’s not gonna happen.”

MUST SEE: Amazing moment as President Trump calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang while he's on stage at the All-In Summit.@POTUS on AI Doomerism: “I'm telling you, it's all a hoax… and we're not going to let that happen.” pic.twitter.com/ZP8cCaSMqG

— The All-In Podcast (@theallinpod) September 14, 2026

Last week, former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon announced his resignation on X / Twitter, accusing both ChatGPT maker OpenAI and Claude maker Anthropic of “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”

“Neither company is acting responsible,” Coxon said. “Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources. We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing.

“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt. If anything, many executives and senior researchers will couch their phrasing in the press to sound sensible — but I hear the same people express fear privately. No other human activity poses this level of danger.”

Coxon said that staff at OpenAI, headed up by Sam Altman, “have not deeply internalized the civilizational stakes,” which is why work to rapidly improve its AI models continues despite the risks. “At Anthropic, the stakes are well-understood, but they are locked in a race to get there first," he insisted. “They believe no one else will act responsibly, so they must do it themselves, despite the risk.”

“Accepting this race and entering the ‘endgame’ is a hubristic gamble that should not be launched from a private company’s Slack. Attempting to speedrun alignment should require extraordinary confidence that there are no better trajectories available.”

Coxon went on to say he was optimistic about the potential for coordination, but doubted AI companies were on track to prevent a global race, “which may require costly actions such as a temporary ban on improving model capabilities.”

He ended his statement by urging AI lab researchers to consider what they were doing. “Do you want to kick off a superintelligent RL run without a rigorous understanding of its mind?” he asked. “Should you put your head down because ‘it’s happening anyway’ - or take this moment to call for different conditions?”

Coxon’s statement sent shockwaves throughout social media, sparking alarm and a string of mainstream headlines. It was backed up by Evan Hubinger, Anthropic’s ‘Alignment Science’ lead, who added an even starker warning.

“Jacob is correct here — we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!" he said. “I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to.”

In recent days, Altman, Anthropic boss Dario Amodei, and Grok boss Elon Musk have all suggested their willingness to work together to slow down AI development. Altman has said this “pacing” would not mean “stopping.” In a social media post, he said: “Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs. Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring. Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.”

In further posts, Trump said the U.S. already has “tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies!”

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” Trump wrote.

He insisted he had already prevented AI companies from doing “bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’” and singled out Anthropic boss Dario Amodei for “now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel.’”

According to CNN, some White House officials are worried about Trump’s lack of concern about the dangers of AI amid growing public skepticism and fear of the technology.

Vice President JD Vance said Monday that the administration is "concerned" about the technology, but said AI companies calling for government oversight feels like a "Trojan horse."

"It's something that we're concerned by, but we want to make sure that we actually regulate smartly, and we're thoughtful about the risk here,” he said. “So, there are obviously risks to AI. There are some benefits to AI. I have to say, just personally, I feel a little bit weird about the fact that you have so many Frontier AI tech companies kind of coming to the government and begging the government to regulate them — it feels a little bit to me like a bit of a Trojan horse.”

Photo by Ludovic MARIN / AFP via Getty Images.

items.title: Is Eternal Darkness Getting a Remaster? Nightdive Studios Raises Hopes That the GameCube Classic Will Return
items.description: Hopes of an Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem remaster have been raised by an intriguing comment from Nightdive Studios.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Hopes of an Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem remaster have been raised by an intriguing comment from Nightdive Studios.

The talented team at Nightdive are port and remaster specialists who have previously dusted off dozens of classic video games for re-release. These include various titles in the System Shock, Quake, Doom and Turok franchises, plus Heretic + Hexen and Thief: The Dark Project.

Now owned by Atari, Nightdive has found an audience with its enhanced ports, which typically receive a lick of visual paint while remaining true to their original forms. And, of course, Nightdive does this in collaboration with the games' original development studio where possible.

Could long-lost classic Eternal Darkness be next? Responding to a fan request via social media yesterday on the 25th anniversary of the GameCube, Nightdive CEO Stephen Kick had this to say: "Eternal Darkness is one of my all-time favorites and it deserves the treatment I know Nightdive Studios is capable of," Kick wrote. "Keep your eye on our Deep Dives..."

Here, Kick is referring to the studio's lengthy videos it releases via YouTube, discussing the various projects it has taken on. Surely this is a suggestion that Eternal Darkness will be next?

Perhaps, though, it's worth remaining cautious until anything is officially announced. Nightdive has attempted to work on Nintendo-published games before, but has never quite got close enough. In 2022, Kick commented that the Mario maker "always get[s] gun shy working with third-party developers," despite discussions to work on an array of its games. One of these was a remaster of the N64 classic Goldeneye 007 that Nintendo ultimately decided against — only to drop the original on Nintendo Switch Online instead. Still, Kick has long maintained that Eternal Darkness is his favorite Nintendo game he'd like Nightdive to work on.

Developed by Silicon Knights, the survival horror adventure launched for the GameCube back in 2002 and became a cult classic for Nintendo fans who were impressed (and suitably freaked out) by the game's creepy sanity mechanics, which Nintendo itself locked down with a patent.

Eternal Darkness sees players controlling an array of characters throughout history, each of which can descend into madness if you're not careful. The psychological effects of this are then experienced by the player, from subtle noises and skewed camera angles, to visual effects such as bleeding walls or moving statues. At its most extreme, the game begins breaking the fourth wall, appearing to reset progress or mute players' TVs. It's enough to make you want to go mad on purpose, just to see how wacky the game gets.

But despite strong reviews, Eternal Darkness sold relatively poorly. Plans for a sequel were discussed for years, though various issues within Silicon Knights hampered progress, and a later push for a spiritual successor via a crowdfunding campaign also fell by the wayside. Silicon Knights ultimately shut down in 2014, while Nintendo's patent for the game's sanity system is now believed to have lapsed.

Is it finally time to descend into madness once more? Here's hoping.

items.title: US Confirms for the First Time It Has Deployed a Space Weapon in Earth's Orbit
items.description: It sounds like something ripped straight out of a science fiction war movie, but it is now a reality: the U.S. has, for the first time, confirmed it has deployed a space weapon in Earth’s orbit.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
It sounds like something ripped straight out of a science fiction war movie, but it is now a reality: the U.S. has, for the first time, confirmed it has deployed a space weapon in Earth’s orbit.

Confirmation comes from Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink, who was speaking at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference on Monday. He insisted the space weapon was about protecting U.S. forces.

As reported by CNN, Meink said:

“Today we continue to ensure we remain ready to meet the challenges of evolving threats wherever they exist. This is why the United States now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.”

“It is critically important that we maintain our dominance not only in the air but in space, and so we’ve had to take steps to make sure that when we’re threatened, we can take care of that,” Meink continued.

Meink refused to explain what the weapon was capable of doing, or when it was put in orbit. Nor do we know if the weapon has already been used.

U.S. officials have hinted at having offensive and defensive space capabilities for some time now, but this is the first time someone has gone on the record to confirm it. There’s a great deal of speculation about what the weapon may be. Some think it could be a kinetic weapon that could actually crash into something, perhaps a satellite, and blow it up. Others think it’s more likely a jammer or a directed energy weapon, one that wouldn’t cause damaging space debris.

The Trump administration has in the past talked about space weapons forming part of the U.S.’s anti-air ‘Golden dome’ defence system, having set up the Space Force in 2019 to work on space capabilities. A spokesperson for the U.S. Space Force told the BBC: "Space control encapsulates the mission areas required to contest and control the space domain — employing kinetic and non-kinetic means to affect adversary capabilities through disruption, degradation and even destruction, if necessary. These capabilities can be employed for offensive and defensive purposes at the direction of combatant commands."

There are some who believe the next war could start in space, with an adversary perhaps taking out a satellite in an action that would disable communications on earth. This could in turn have a significant impact on a country’s military operations. Space weapons could also theoretically be used to knock long-range missiles that enter orbit out of their trajectory.

The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans weapons of mass destruction in orbit, but it does not prohibit the use of conventional weapons in space or the use of ground-based weapons against assets in space.

Last year, Donald Trump signed an executive order calling U.S superiority in space “a measure of national vision and willpower.” Speaking at the conference, Meink said a U.S. space-based interceptor program had moved “from initial contract to flight-ready hardware in less than one year.”

items.title: James Bond Game 007 First Light Delayed Until 2027 on Nintendo Switch 2
items.description: James Bond game 007 First Light has been delayed yet again on Nintendo Switch 2, and will now arrive in March 2027.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
James Bond game 007 First Light has been delayed yet again on Nintendo Switch 2, and will now arrive in March 2027.

007 First Light was originally expected to land back in May this year on all platforms simultaneously. In April, however, Hitman developer IO Interactive announced a last-minute delay for the Switch 2 version, and stated it would now arrive this fall.

Well, that date has also now fallen through, with a further, lengthy delay until its new release window next March. In a statement posted to social media this morning, IO said it would provide an exact release date nearer the time.

"We know many of you have been looking forward to experiencing Bond's reimagined origin story on Nintendo Switch 2, and we greatly appreciate your enthusiasm," IO wrote. "To ensure we deliver the quality of experience players expect, we have made the decision to delay the release to March 2027, with the exact date to be communicated later. This additional time will go toward polishing the Nintendo Switch 2 performance of the game.

"We were thrilled by the positive feedback on 007 First Light at Gamescom, and it's a great sign of the progress being made across the whole game as we head toward launch," IO continued. "The same demo will be playable at Tokyo Game Show this week, so please join us there if you would like a hands-on experience.

"We will share further updates as soon as we are ready. Thank you for your patience, understanding, and continued support."

For the majority of fans, popping over to Tokyo this week to try the Switch 2 version will likely seem a little excessive. And yet again, it's unclear why the game's Switch 2 version has been delayed relatively close to its expected release. If the game isn't struggling technically, is this a decision made to launch the title when the console has a larger userbase? Is there are fear of arriving too close to GTA 6? And what are the trade-offs to waiting even longer, as hype for the game dies down? IO has not said.

IO announced the news today alongside a fresh update for First Light on PC, which adds path tracing and DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support, in a bid for even more impressive lighting, shadows and reflections. Other upcoming additions include a new story DLC centered around Bawama, the pirate king warlord played by Lenny Kravitz, plus additional TacSim challenges, a fresh gadget, New Game+, and a photo mode.

Since launch, the game has shifted a solid 4 million copies in three months, though IO itself has been rocked by layoffs as Microsoft pulled funding for its fantasy game project. There has also been confusion over what will become of First Light's planned sequels following Amazon's acquisition of the James Bond license.

"Demonstrably obsessed with bringing the Bond fantasy to life in a way no one has ever managed before, 007 First Light is the best Bond game I’ve ever played," IGN wrote in our 007 First Light review, awarding the game a 009/10.

items.title: Marvel's Wolverine Actor Liam McIntyre Isn't Fazed by Players' Brutal Comments About the Game
items.description: Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has seen what fans are saying about him and Insomniac's latest superhero game, but it's no skin off his nose.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has seen what fans are saying about him and Insomniac's latest superhero game, but it's no skin off his nose.

Marvel’s Wolverine is out in the wild for many players worldwide, and opinions have been strong, to say the least. Discourse around the game has been unavoidable over the last month, with a vocal swath of players taking issue with Insomniac’s art direction, character design, and gameplay segments that were shown off by the media and early reviews.

One of the core topics of the Wolverine debate is actor Liam McIntyre, who plays the game’s titular character. Some fans don’t believe he bears a close enough resemblance to the iconic mutant, while others feel that Insomniac’s face scans and art style didn’t do his visage justice.

McIntyre has been excitedly posting about his role as Wolverine ever since his involvement was first announced, and some players have just now realized that he’s been seeing what they’re saying about him on social media this entire time.

In response to one of these players, McIntyre lightheartedly remarked that he’s seen much worse said about him ever since he started his acting career.

“Ha. Man, my career started with the responsibility of taking over for the incredible Andy Whitfield in Spartacus (RIP to that legend). I've read things you couldn't believe :) I just hope everyone has fun. I'm proud as hell of this game. It's a blast,” he wrote on X.

Ha. Man my career started with the responsibility of taking over for the incredible Andy Whitfield in Spartacus (RIP to that legend). I've read things you couldn't believe :)
I just hope everyone has fun. I'm proud as hell of this game. It's a blast. https://t.co/ICtoZhKXEq

— liam (@Liam_J_McIntyre) September 14, 2026

McIntyre did, indeed, play the historical Spartacus in Starz’s 2010s miniseries of the same name. The late great Andy Whitfield notably played the role of Spartacus in the show’s first season, Blood and Sand, but was diagnosed with stage IV non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a type of cancer that affects the blood, before the second season was filmed.

After his death in 2011, McIntyre was tasked with taking over the role — something that sparked strong reactions from fans at the time, though many now remember his time in the show fondly.

All that is to say, McIntyre is no stranger to vocal opinions from fans in response to taking on the mantle of iconic characters who are known to be played by a certain actor. Wolverine has been portrayed by Hugh Jackman in nearly all modern mainline X-Men films, and McIntyre’s take on the character is a big change for viewers who are used to seeing Jackman on screen — but McIntyre is excited for players to experience his version of the grizzled mutant, come what may.

I don't know what the fates have in store for us tomorrow, but I just want to say thank you to everyone for this once in a lifetime opportunity. Thank you to @MarvelGames and @insomniacgames for trusting me with such a beloved character. I'm so proud. What a journey. pic.twitter.com/xVA3iSbJr6

— liam (@Liam_J_McIntyre) September 10, 2026

Marvel’s Wolverine has been met with mixed reviews from critics; IGN gave the game a six out of 10, calling it “standard superhero fare” whose “slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion.”

The game is officially coming out tonight for all players, so if you're keen on playing it, tell us what you think about it in the comments below. Does it live up to the hype, or do you think Insomniac's latest offering doesn't break the mold enough to warrant a standout review?

items.title: Wardogs Players Are Avoiding One of the Game's Factions Because It Has a Stigma of Attracting the Stupidest Players
items.description: Wardogs players are avoiding the game's Lonestar faction, as they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Wardogs players are avoiding the game's Lonestar faction, as they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games.

There are three playable teams in Wardogs: a blue team (Lonestar), a red team (Valkyra), and a green team (Manticore). The different teams don't really have any major gameplay effects, but there is a stigma around Lonestar. For whatever reason, Lonestar has a really difficult time accomplishing much of anything in Wardogs. The team tends to attract the worst and newest players, leading to a major handicap for players on that team. There are a lot of theories as to why this is happening, with one being that it's the first option, so new players pick it by default.

Other teams also fill up extremely quickly because of the stigma, meaning more inexperienced players who don't know any better are sometimes shut out of having other options. One player on Reddit noted that some matches have delayed starts, simply because some players refuse to pick Lonestar, and it leads to the game not starting the match due to a lack of players. You can see one viral clip of Lonestar's antics below to get an idea of the absurdity that some players are experiencing.

I love everything about this clip.

Never change Blues 💙

(Thanks to u/pancakerulez for sharing) pic.twitter.com/BvWsRtOd6q

— Lossy (@L0SSY) September 14, 2026

There are instances of Lonestar overcoming the odds and proving the doubters wrong. In my experience, I have never won on Lonestar. All of my wins in Wardogs come from playing with the other two teams. Is that a coincidence? It seems statistically unlikely, but maybe! Hopefully this will iron out as the game's player base becomes more experienced and more well-rounded, but who's to say when that will happen.

Wardogs has been a breakout hit, selling a million copies prior to launch and sitting near the top of Steam's most-played games. The positive word of mouth keeps attracting new players, and that will likely continue over the next few weeks and months, especially as the game already has a slight discount through Fanatical. If you're a console player hoping to get in on the action, you'll have to wait a while. Wardogs is planned to release on Xbox and PS5 in 2028, so don't expect it anytime soon.
